board: AG32VF303CCT6 / L48, SRAM configuration through a single controlled board client

unproven_shape_20260929.definition: Fabric ROUTE pip whose shape (source mux family and index, destination mux family and index, dx, dy) is used by no board-passing open image and no shipped silicon-qualified routed fixture, anywhere on the device.
unproven_shape_20260929.proven_evidence: 146,255 distinct pips from 2,141 board-passing open images with retained routed netlists plus 75 shipped qualified routed fixtures; 4,183 proven shapes. Placement-keystone experiments are not counted as proof.
unproven_shape_20260929.policy: Post-route refusal plus the existing retry penalty. The device graph and every profile identity are unchanged. A shape becomes admissible once a design-level silicon pass uses it.

board_pair_20260929.definition: Pips present in both failing fast-RAM images of one placement and absent from a 98%-same-placement passing image of the same source.

17/18 PASS, LFSR RATE_FAIL, all 19 references PASS; every design without never-proven-shape pips passed

limitations: Finite reset-trial repeatability on one board at 10 MHz; not a temperature, voltage or cross-board qualification.

The refusal targets an evidence class, not a proven physical mechanism. Many proven-shape pips are still unwitnessed at their exact coordinate, and the fast-RAM case needed 15 additional pair-isolated pips.
A design whose only legal route needs a refused pip fails to build rather than emitting an image; that is containment, not support.
Historical failed images were not used as negative evidence because their causes are mixed.
